chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from ʿAli ibn Asbat, from ʿAli ibn Salim, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, he said:

I said to him: “Should I perform tayammum and pray, then afterward find water while there is still time remaining for me?” He said: “Do not repeat the salat, for indeed the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth.”

Then Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi said to him: “Should I search for water to the right and to the left?” He said: “Do not search, neither to the right nor to the left, nor in a well. If you find it on the road, then perform wudu (ablution) with it; and if you do not find it, then proceed.”
Thus, the proper understanding of this report is the state of fear and necessity. But when excuses are absent, then seeking is unavoidable, in accordance with what the first report contained.

key_terms.أَتَيَمَّمُ: I perform tayammum as a substitute purification when water is unavailable
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the prescribed salat whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity that justifies relaxation in the ruling
key_terms.الطَّلَبِ: seeking water before resorting to tayammum
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: a state of fear that affects the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water required for wudu (ablution) or purification
key_terms.فَتَوَضَّأْ: perform wudu (ablution) with the water if it is found

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the time ends, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of tayammum when water is unavailable and clarifies that a prayer performed with tayammum does not need to be repeated if water is found afterward within the prayer time. It also indicates that the instruction not to search extensively for water is understood in the context of fear and necessity, while ordinarily one must seek water before resorting to tayammum.
